key_insight: NH4SCN enables high-n quasi-2D perovskite scaffolds to template highly (110)-ordered 3D MAPbI3, rather than primarily aiding charge transport through vertically oriented 2D layers.
engineering_relevance: Controlling crystallisation kinetics and scaffold–3D lattice matching offers a route to improved perovskite absorber structure for solar cells.
method: Use NH4SCN to extend the nucleation window, suppressing n = 1 phases and promoting high-n scaffolds.
Probe phase formation and structural ordering with spectroscopic and structural studies.
Assess lattice matching and cation dependence of scaffold-mediated MAPbI3 growth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust structural evidence of highly (110)-ordered MAPbI3 and close lattice matching with quasi-2D phases, but provides no quantitative device-performance metrics.
watch_item: The templating effect is cation dependent and requires both close lattice matching and effective kinetic control of the relevant quasi-2D phases.
paper_title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
